newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-DBS Land sets A$200 mln programme.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-DBS Land sets A$200 mln programme.

text.p: Singapore's DBS Land Ltd said on Tuesday that it has established an A$200 million domestic medium term note programme.
It also announced a debut A$81 million issue off the programme.
The three-year notes, which will be issued in kangaroo form, will be priced at 30 basis points over the 90 day bank bill swap rate (BBSW).

The programme, the first to be established by a Singaporean borrower, and issue are arranged and lead managed by SBC Warburg in Singapore and Australia. Co-managers to the issue are DBS Bank, Singapore and Westdeutsche Landesbank, Singapore.

The programme and issue for DBS Land, one of the largest listed property developers and landlords in Singapore, is a key element in its business acitivity and geographic diversification, said SBC Warburg in a statement.
"This issue is further testament to the attraction of the Australian dollar market for foreign issuers," said Ron Ogden, Executive Director Rates Origination at SBC Warburg.

"Following recent issues by Fannie Mae of the United States, and issues by a number of other offshore issuers, the appeal of the Australian market, across the credit spectrum from all around the world, is clear," Ogden added.
Earlier this year Fannie Mae issued two A$1.0 billion global bonds in five and 10-year maturities.
